newsitem.title: ITALY: Greenshoe option on Italy's Eni seen likely.
newsitem.headline: Greenshoe option on Italy's Eni seen likely.

text.p: Italy is likely to use up an over-allotment, or "greenshoe" option placed on the second tranche sale of shares in energy group Eni, Treasury director general Mario Draghi said on Thursday.
"If the greenshoe is used up, and it would reasonable to assume this, then the global Eni offering will end up 80 percent larger than originally planned," Draghi told a Euromoney conference.
A total 165 million additional shares were put in the greenshoe reserve.
The Treasury raised 7.698 trillion lire from the sale of 14 percent of its stake in the oil and chemicals group last month.
If all the greenshoe is sold the Treasury would raise a total 8.88 trillion lire from the second tranche sale.
Originally Italy planned to sell just 700 million shares. If the greenshoe is allocated it will end up having sold well over 1.2 billion shares.
